sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Ag–Ni binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset AgNi-04Din.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, L2 → L1 + (Ni), lies at 1703.4 K.
The Ag–Ni system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as miscibility gap, monotectic.
The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of A.T. Dinsdale, unpublished, 2004. [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
At 1703.4 K the monotectic L2 → L1 + (Ni) takes place; the L1 phase then contains 3.8 at.%.
We obtain 1234.2 K for the eutectic reaction (L → (Ag) + (Ni)), where L has 0.3 at.% Ni.
According to Table 2, (Ag) remains stable up to 1234.9 K (melting of the pure element).
The solubility of Ag in (Ni) reaches 1.0 at.% at 1703.4 K.
At 2600 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its maximum, 15118 J/mol, at 38.0 at.% Ni.
For the equiatomic liquid at 2600 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −3.88 kJ/mol-atom.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
